videos.title: How America Moved Giant Logs Before Trucks
videos.description:
Before trucks, bulldozers, or chainsaws, America was built on the backs of men who hauled 400-ton trees out of the deepest forests using oxen, water, steam, and pure ingenuity. 🌲 From the river pigs dancing across churning logs to the high climbers risking their lives 200 feet in the air, this is the forgotten story of how the biggest trees on the continent were moved, the wild machines that made it possible, and the hidden cost paid by the forests and the men who worked them. ⚙️🪓

videos.description:

From ingenious engineering to environmental destruction, this is one of the wildest stories in American industrial history.

videos.title: How America Built Entire Towns Just to Mine One Mountain
videos.description:
How mining shaped the American West - and why so many boomtowns became ghost towns. This video explores the rise and collapse of places like Cripple Creek, Butte, and Bisbee, revealing how company towns were built around gold, silver, and copper - then abandoned when the money ran out. ⛏️🏔️

From explosive growth to labor abuse, environmental ruin, and forgotten streets in the desert, this is the hidden story of America’s mining empire and the people it left behind.
